newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Power failure shuts Taiwan CPC's No.5 cracker.
newsitem.headline: Power failure shuts Taiwan CPC's No.5 cracker.

text.p: Taiwan state oil monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp on Thursday shut down its No.5 naphtha cracker in Kaohsiung due to a power failure but said it expected normal operations to resume by Saturday.
"We halted the No.5 naphtha cracker after an unexpected power failure caused by Taipower," an executve in Taipei said by telephone. Taiwan Power Co is Taiwan's main electrical utility.
The power outage lasted just one minute, officials said.
The Chinese Petroleum executive said operators would try to resume normal functions of the cracker by Saturday.
"We are starting to turn on plants that were affected by the power failure," the official said.
Chinese Petroleum's No.5 cracker has an annual production capacity of 400,000 tonnes of ethylene.
Twenty of the Kaohsiung refinery's 36 petroleum and chemical plants had to be shut down because of the power failure, an official at the Kaohsiung refinery said by telephone.
"Taipower's power supply was disrupted for about one minute earlier this morning and forced us to take emergency shut down procedures to close 20 plants," the Kaohsiung official said.
"The Kaohsiung refinery took emergency shut down measures after our system detected that the power supply was disrupted," he said.
No estimate of damage or losses were available and it was not known whether Chinese Petroleum would seek compensation from Taipower.
Chinese Petroleum operates two other crackers. Its No.3 cracker has an annual production capacity of 230,000 tonnes of ethylene and its No.4 cracker has a 385,000 tonne capacity.
